en: to be enrolled; to be registered as a member

examples.ko: 보험에 가입돼 있어서 비용은 걱정 안 해도 돼요.
examples.en: I'm enrolled in insurance, so I don't need to worry about the cost.
When you are signed up as a member, an email arrives.
I got a text saying I've been signed up for the club.
This number isn't registered yet.

examples.ko: 이 번호로는 이미 가입된 계정이 있어요.
examples.en: There is already an account registered with this number.
I got a coupon right after I was signed up.

explain: '가입하다'는 내가 신청하는 행동이고, '가입되다'는 신청이 끝나 회원이 된 상태예요. 앱, 보험, 동아리에서 써요. '가입돼 있다'는 지금 회원이라는 말로 가장 자주 나와요. 반대는 '탈퇴하다'예요.

phrases.example: 저는 이 앱에 이미 가입돼 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm already signed up for this app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 회원인 상태를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say you are currently a member.

phrases.en: The email was wrong, so I haven't signed up yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신청이 끝나지 않아 아직 회원이 아닐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the sign-up isn't finished and you're not yet a member.

phrases.en: If you make a card, you are automatically enrolled in insurance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따로 신청하지 않아도 회원이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you become a member without applying separately.

explain_en: 가입하다 is the action of applying, and 가입되다 is the state after you have become a member. It is used for apps, insurance, and clubs. 가입돼 있다 is the most common form for being a member now. The opposite is 탈퇴하다.

examples.en: The ID card is issued within a week.
The passport was issued yesterday.
I will send you a text once the document is issued.
You have to wait until the card is issued.

examples.ko: 발급되는 데 보통 삼 일쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It usually takes about three days to be issued.
The certificate was issued wrongly, so I applied again.

explain: 발급되다는 증명서, 여권, 카드처럼 관청이나 회사가 만들어 주는 서류에 써요. 주어는 서류예요. 서류를 만들어 주는 쪽은 '발급하다', 받는 쪽은 '발급받다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The card will be issued next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 서류가 나올 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a document that will be issued in the future.

phrases.en: The document hasn't been issued yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 서류가 나오지 않았을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for when a document hasn't come out yet.

phrases.en: The ID is issued right away when you apply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기다리지 않고 빨리 나온다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it comes out quickly without waiting.

explain_en: 발급되다 is for documents that an office or company produces, such as certificates, passports and cards; the subject is the document. The issuing side uses '발급하다' and the receiving side uses '발급받다'.

examples.en: You have to renew your driver's license before it expires.

examples.ko: 운전면허증을 집에 두고 와서 렌터카를 못 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I left my driver's license at home, so I couldn't rent a car.
I don't like the photo on my driver's license.

examples.ko: 신분증 대신 운전면허증으로도 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also verify with a driver's license instead of an ID card.
I don't have a driver's license, so I take the bus.
The address on my driver's license is still the old one.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 '면허증'이나 '면허'라고 많이 말해요. '면허를 따다'(취득하다), '면허를 갱신하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사를 알아 두세요. 신분증 대신 내밀 수 있는 카드이기도 해요.

phrases.en: I kept my license in my wallet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '운전면허증'을 줄인 말로, 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 운전면허증 that is common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I got my driver's license last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험에 합격해서 면허를 얻을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual verb phrase for obtaining a license by passing the test.

phrases.en: The police officer asked me to show my license.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신분이나 운전 자격을 확인할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone checks your ID or driving qualification.

explain_en: In daily talk people shorten it to '면허증' or '면허'. Learn the common verbs, such as '면허를 따다' (get a license) and '면허를 갱신하다' (renew it). It can also serve as an ID card.

en: to prove; to demonstrate; to certify with evidence

examples.en: I prove that I am a student.
This document proves my age.
He proved his skill at the competition.
I'll prove it with results rather than words.
Is there a way to prove it?

examples.ko: 신분을 증명할 수 있는 카드가 필요해요.
examples.en: You need a card that can prove your identity.

explain: '증명하다'는 서류나 결과로 사실을 보여 줄 때 써요. 신분이나 나이는 '신분증으로 증명하다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 '확인하다'는 맞는지 살펴보는 쪽이에요.

phrases.example: 이 사진이 제 말을 증명할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This photo can prove what I said.
phrases.nuance_ko: 근거가 있을 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have evidence.

phrases.en: I need a graduation certificate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실을 공식적으로 보여 주는 서류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A document that officially shows a fact.

phrases.en: Please prove your age with an ID card.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇으로 증명하는지 '~(으)로'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say how you prove it with '~(으)로'.

explain_en: 증명하다 is used when you show that something is true through documents or results. For identity or age you say '신분증으로 증명하다' (prove with an ID). The similar 확인하다 leans toward checking whether something is correct.

t90.ax: Is there a way to prove it?

en: to be approved; to be consented; to be permitted

examples.ko: 이곳에서는 사진 찍는 것이 허락되지 않아요.
examples.en: Taking photos is not permitted here.
My vacation was finally approved.
Going out is allowed until ten at night.
Only permitted people can enter.
With your parents' consent, it will be allowed.
I was really happy that my admission was approved.

explain: '허락하다'는 허락해 주는 사람이 중심이고, '허락되다'는 허락을 받은 결과를 말해요. '허용되다'가 규칙이 정해서 되는 것이라면 '허락되다'는 어떤 사람이 되게 해 준 느낌이에요. 일상에서는 '허락을 받다', '돼요'를 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Would it be allowed for me to leave early today?
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락을 받을 수 있는지 조심스럽게 묻는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a careful way to ask whether permission will be given.

phrases.en: I got permission from my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '허락되다'보다 더 자주 써요. 받은 사람이 중심이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is more common in daily life than '허락되다'. The focus is on the person who received permission.

phrases.en: I'm glad that going out was allowed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어서'로 허락된 결과 때문에 생긴 기분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-a/eoseo' you give the feeling that came from the permission.

explain_en: 허락하다 centers on the person granting permission, while 허락되다 states the result of being permitted. 허용되다 feels like a rule allows it, whereas 허락되다 feels like a person let it happen. In daily talk, '허락을 받다' and plain 돼요 are more common.

gh: officially licensed by authorities, e.g. a school
formally approved after review, plan or request

p.n: Approval is for requests or plans, so it is unnatural for personal permission.

examples.en: You need a screwdriver to loosen the screw.
My father fixed the chair with a screwdriver.

examples.ko: 작은 드라이버 좀 빌려줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can you lend me a small screwdriver?
I took a Phillips screwdriver out of the toolbox drawer.

examples.ko: 드라이버는 서랍 맨 위 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The screwdriver is in the top compartment of the drawer.

examples.ko: 안경 나사는 작은 드라이버만 돌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only a small screwdriver can turn the screws of glasses.

explain: 나사를 돌리는 공구 말고도, 골프의 드라이버나 컴퓨터의 장치 드라이버도 소리가 같아요. 자동차를 운전하는 사람은 '운전자'나 '기사'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please lend me a Phillips screwdriver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 십자 모양 나사에 쓰는 드라이버예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A screwdriver for cross-shaped screws.

phrases.en: I tighten the screw firmly with a screwdriver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나사를 돌려 단단하게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for turning a screw until it is tight.

phrases.en: I borrowed a screwdriver from my neighbor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공구가 없을 때 흔히 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common thing to say when you don't have the tool.

explain_en: Besides the tool that turns screws, a golf driver and a computer device driver are pronounced the same. A person who drives a car is called '운전자' or '기사'.

examples.ko: 새 매트리스를 사고 나서 잘 자요.
examples.en: I sleep well since I bought a new mattress.
The mattress was so hard that my back hurt.
This bed sells the mattress separately.
I spread a clean sheet on the mattress.
The hotel mattress was soft and nice.
Putting a cover on the mattress made it look neat.

explain: 침대에서 몸이 닿는 푹신한 부분을 말해요. 이불은 위에 덮고, 매트리스는 아래에 깔아요.

phrases.en: I laid a mattress on the floor and slept.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이불처럼 위에 덮는 것이 아니라 아래에 까는 물건이라서 '깔다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mattresses go underneath, not on top like a blanket, so you use '깔다'.

phrases.en: This mattress is soft, so it is comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매트리스의 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how a mattress feels.

phrases.en: My back hurt, so I changed my mattress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새것으로 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when replacing it with a new one.

explain_en: It is the soft part of a bed that your body rests on. A blanket goes on top, while the mattress goes underneath.

examples.en: This phone is short on memory.
I want to add more memory to my computer.
If you delete photos, you get memory space.
I put a memory card into the new camera.

examples.ko: 메모리 용량이 큰 제품을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a product with large memory capacity.

examples.ko: 앱을 많이 켜 두면 메모리 때문에 느려져요.
examples.en: If you keep many apps open, it slows down because of memory.

explain: 컴퓨터와 휴대폰에서 저장 공간과 작업 공간을 둘 다 '메모리'라고 불러서 헷갈릴 수 있어요. 사진과 앱이 차지하는 쪽은 '저장 공간'이나 '용량'이라고도 말해요. 사람의 기억은 '기억'이나 '추억'이고, 메모리는 기계 쪽에만 써요.

phrases.en: I saved the photos on a memory card.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카메라나 휴대폰에 넣는 작은 저장 카드를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small storage card put into a camera or phone.

phrases.en: I deleted apps because I ran out of storage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진과 앱이 차지하는 공간은 '메모리'보다 '저장 공간'이 더 정확해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For space used by photos and apps, 'storage space' is more precise than 'memory'.

phrases.en: I bought a phone with a large memory capacity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼마나 많이 담을 수 있는지를 말할 때 '용량'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'capacity' to say how much it can hold.

explain_en: On computers and phones both storage and working space are called 'memory', which can be confusing. For what photos and apps take up, people also say '저장 공간' or '용량'. A person's memories are '기억' or '추억'; 'memory' here is only for machines.

gh: fond, nostalgic memory of the past

p.n: Not interchangeable. 메모리 is computer memory and 기억 cannot be used for it.

t90.ax: This phone is short on memory.

en: to set; to configure; to establish

examples.en: I set the phone alarm to seven.
I set a new password.
Do not set your goal too high.
It takes long because there are many items to configure.
The screen I set up has changed.
I use it with the language set to Korean.

explain: 앱과 기계에서는 '설정'이 메뉴 이름으로도 쓰여서 '설정에서 바꾸세요'라고 자주 말해요. 목표나 기준을 정한다는 뜻으로도 써요. '정하다'보다 기계나 공식적인 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I set my goal for this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준이나 목표를 정할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when setting a standard or goal.

phrases.en: I changed the app settings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '설정'은 앱이나 기계의 메뉴 이름으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 설정 is often used as a menu name in apps and devices.

phrases.en: We decide the meeting time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '설정하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 설정하다 and more natural in daily talk.

explain_en: Setting is also the name of the menu in apps and devices, so people often say 'change it in Settings'. It also means to fix a goal or standard. It feels more technical or formal than the plain verb for deciding.

examples.en: I forgot the phone number, so I looked through the phone directory.
In the old days every house had a thick phone directory.
I looked up the hospital's number in the phone directory.
The shop's number wasn't in the phone directory.

examples.ko: 스마트폰 전화번호부에 저장된 사람이 삼백 명이나 돼요.
examples.en: There are as many as three hundred people saved in my smartphone's phone book.
I threw away the old phone directory when I moved.

explain: 종이로 된 두꺼운 책을 떠올리게 하지만, 스마트폰 안의 연락처 목록을 가리킬 때도 써요. 폰 이야기에서는 '연락처'라고도 많이 해요.

phrases.en: Look for it in your phone contacts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스마트폰 이야기에서는 '전화번호부' 대신 '연락처'를 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: When talking about smartphones, '연락처' is used more than '전화번호부'.

phrases.en: I found the hospital's number in the phone directory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 번호를 찾을 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for looking up a number.
phrases.en_equiv: to look up in the directory

phrases.en: Old houses had a thick phone directory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이로 된 책 모양의 전화번호부를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the thick, printed book version of the directory.

explain_en: It brings to mind a thick paper book, but it can also refer to the contact list inside a smartphone. When talking about phones, people often say '연락처' too.

examples.en: I received a movie ticket as a gift.
Please show your ticket at the entrance.
I have one museum ticket left.
How much is one ticket?

examples.ko: 친구가 공연 관람권을 두 장 보내 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend sent me two tickets to a show.

examples.ko: 이 관람권으로 전시를 두 번 볼 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can I see the exhibition twice with this ticket?

explain: 영화나 전시, 공연을 보러 들어갈 수 있는 표예요. '영화 관람권'처럼 선물이나 쿠폰으로 받는 표에 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '표'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I bought two tickets for the performance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 영화, 공연, 전시를 붙여 어떤 표인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put movie, performance or exhibition in front to say what kind of ticket.

phrases.en: Please show your ticket at the entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: I booked the exhibition tickets in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 표를 사 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when buying a ticket in advance.

explain_en: It is a ticket that lets you in to see a movie, exhibition or show. It is often used for gifted or coupon-style tickets, like '영화 관람권'. In daily talk people also just say '표'.

examples.en: I always freeze leftover rice.
I bought meat and froze it right away.

examples.ko: 이 생선은 오늘 밤에 냉동할 거예요.
examples.en: I will freeze this fish tonight.
I looked up how to freeze it on the internet.
After freezing the bread, I put it in a plastic bag.
I froze the fruit and made juice out of it.

explain: '냉동'은 얼리는 것이고 '냉장'은 차갑게 두는 것이라서 서로 달라요. 냉장고의 얼리는 칸은 '냉동실', 차가운 칸은 '냉장실'이에요. '냉동식품'처럼 명사 앞에도 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: I put the leftover bread in the freezer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냉동하는 장소를 함께 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the place where things are frozen.

phrases.en: I freeze water to make ice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '냉동하다'보다 쉬운 말이고, 물이나 음식에 모두 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 'naengdonghada' and used for water or food.

phrases.en: When I'm busy, I eat frozen food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼려서 파는 음식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to food sold frozen.

explain_en: '냉동' means freezing and '냉장' means keeping chilled, so they differ. In a fridge the freezer part is '냉동실' and the cool part is '냉장실'. It also attaches to nouns, as in '냉동식품'.

examples.en: Write your name on the answer sheet first.
Time was up, so I handed in my answer sheet.

examples.ko: 답안지 칸을 잘못 칠해서 다시 썼어요.
examples.en: I filled in the wrong box on the answer sheet and redid it.
The teacher collected the answer sheets.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나면 답안지는 뒤에서 앞으로 넘겨요.
examples.en: When the exam ends, we pass the answer sheets from back to front.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터로 채점하는 답안지에는 연필로 써야 해요.
examples.en: On a machine-graded answer sheet you have to write in pencil.

explain: 문제가 적힌 '시험지'와 달리, 답을 쓰거나 표시하는 종이가 '답안지'예요. '답안지를 내다/제출하다/작성하다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: When the bell rang, I handed in my answer sheet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험이 끝나고 제출할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most common when handing in after an exam.
phrases.en_equiv: to hand in the answer sheet

phrases.example: 답안지를 작성할 때는 검은 펜을 쓰세요.
phrases.en: Use a black pen when filling out the answer sheet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 격식 있게 쓸 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a slightly more formal context.
phrases.en_equiv: to fill out the answer sheet

phrases.en: Write your answers on the answer sheet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 답을 쓰는 곳을 말할 때 '에'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 에 to say where the answer goes.
phrases.en_equiv: to write on the answer sheet

explain_en: Unlike the '시험지' (the paper with questions), the '답안지' is the paper where you write or mark answers. It goes with '답안지를 내다/제출하다/작성하다'.

en: to lend out; to take out a loan

examples.en: I borrowed three books from the library.

examples.ko: 은행이 저에게 집 살 돈을 대출했어요.
examples.en: The bank lent me money to buy a house.

examples.ko: 신분증이 있으면 책을 대출할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can borrow books if you have an ID.

examples.ko: 은행은 돈을 대출해 줄 때 서류를 확인해요.
examples.en: Banks check documents when they lend money.
The borrowing period is two weeks.

examples.ko: 대출한 책은 다음 주까지 돌려줘야 해요.
examples.en: You must return the borrowed book by next week.

explain: '대출하다'는 도서관에서는 책을 빌릴 때도 빌려줄 때도 써요. 은행에서는 돈을 빌려주는 쪽이 '대출하다', 빌리는 쪽이 '대출받다'예요. 책은 '대출', '반납'으로 말하고, 은행 돈은 '대출을 받다', '갚다'로 말해요. 일상에서 '책을 빌리다'가 가장 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I took out a loan from the bank to buy a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 빌리는 쪽이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by the person who borrows the money.

phrases.en: The bank lent me money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빌려주는 쪽이 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes what the lending side does.

phrases.en: I want to borrow a comic book from the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도서관 직원에게 책을 빌리고 싶다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell library staff you want to borrow a book.

explain_en: At a library, 대출하다 is used both for borrowing and lending a book. At a bank, the lender 대출하다 and the borrower says 대출받다. Library books go with 대출 and 반납, bank money with 대출을 받다 and 갚다. In everyday speech, '책을 빌리다' is the most natural way to say you borrowed a book.
